chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Shu'ayb al-Haddad, from Bashar ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sells goods on credit, then buys them back from the owner from whom he had sold them. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no problem with it.' So I said to him, 'Can I buy my own goods?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not your goods, nor your cow, nor your sheep.'
Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Shu'ayb al-Haddad, from Bashar ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem with it / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell goods on credit and buy them back for cash at a lower price in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of *bay' al-inah* (selling on credit and buying back for cash) through Imam al-Sadiq (AS), who validates the transaction while distinguishing the repurchased item as a new acquisition rather than a mere return of the original owner's property. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for validating commercial flexibility, though it is often discussed alongside the Hanafi view and the potential for *riba* (usury) if structured as a disguised loan. The clarification that the goods are not 'your goods' nor 'your cattle' emphasizes the legal separation of the two distinct sales contracts involved.
